nodes.title: Neutral fibre data
nodes.statement: A neutral fibre datum over a field k consists of an essentially small k-linear abelian rigid symmetric monoidal category C, a specified isomorphism k ≃ End_C(1), and a k-linear exact faithful strong symmetric monoidal functor ω:C→Vect_fd(k). The symmetry is the one that ω preserves. This datum contains neither a representing group nor a Hopf algebra.
hypotheses: k is a field; category and Hom universes are fixed; Vect_fd(k) consists of finite-dimensional k-vector spaces with ordinary tensor symmetry.
proofSteps: Use existing Abelian, Linear, RigidCategory and monoidal-functor structures; exactness means preserving short exact sequences.
Identify End(1) with k by the specified scalar map and check its compatibility with ω.
Supply scalar extension ω_R(X)=R⊗_kω(X), with its induced strong symmetric monoidal structure, for every commutative k-algebra R.

sources.match: Input data for reconstruction, before any Hopf algebra is known.

acceptance: Do not infer neutrality from a fibre functor over a field extension.
The subquotient-sum hull used by the existing finite representer is distinguished from the tensor hull.

api.name: NeutralFibreData.baseChange
api.statement: For each k-algebra R, ω_R is a strong symmetric monoidal functor into finite projective R-modules; algebra maps induce coherent base change.

api.name: NeutralFibreData.finiteLength
api.statement: Every object has finite length, bounded by dim_k ω(X), using exact faithfulness.

api.name: NeutralFibreData.reflectIso
api.statement: A morphism whose fibre is invertible is invertible; a zero fibre detects the zero object.

api.name: NeutralFibreData.tensorEquiv
api.statement: A k-linear symmetric monoidal equivalence carrying ω to ωprime transports the datum and all tensor automorphism functors.

tests.name: neutral_vect
tests.statement: Vect_fd(k) with the identity functor is neutral and reconstructs the trivial group.

tests.name: neutral_super_sign
tests.statement: Super vector spaces in characteristic different from 2 with Koszul symmetry and ordinary forgetful functor fail symmetric compatibility on the odd line: its self-symmetry is minus the identity.

tests.name: neutral_projectives
tests.statement: Finite free Z-modules are not an abelian category: multiplication by 2 is both a monomorphism and an epimorphism there but is not invertible. Moreover Z is not a field, so this is not the field-valued datum.

tests.name: neutral_not_semisimple
tests.statement: Rep_fd(F_p,C_p) with its forgetful fibre is neutral even though the regular representation is not semisimple.

uses.how: Supply the finite-length and exact-faithful input without presupposing a Hopf algebra.
Record the exact neutrality and symmetry hypotheses that Satake must prove.

nodes.title: Relative reconstruction data
nodes.statement: Let A be an essentially small rigid symmetric monoidal category. A relative reconstruction datum consists of a symmetric monoidal category C with coherent tensor A-action, a conservative A-linear strong symmetric monoidal functor F:C→A, and a small filtered full exhaustion C_i of C stable under A-action and F-split coequalizers. Each C_i has X_i and A-enriched representability: Hom_Ci(V⊙X_i,Y) ≃ Hom_A(V,F_iY), natural in V∈A and Y∈C_i and compatible with the action. Require existence and reflection of the indicated coequalizers. Preservation is an additional named hypothesis for the strengthened theorem, not part of the printed FS datum.
hypotheses: F-split means that the image parallel pair is part of a split coequalizer diagram in A.
Transition functors are full inclusions compatible with F; objects of A are viewed as compact representables in Ind(A). The tensor on Ind(A) is the filtered-colimit-preserving extension of that on A.
proofSteps: Spell out action associator and unit, the symmetric interchange with C tensor, and F(V⊙Y) ≃ V⊗F(Y), with their coherence squares.
The representing isomorphism is a natural bijection of Hom sets for every V, not a claimed isomorphism between a set and an A-object.
Use filtered inclusions to define comparison maps of representers; construct the Ind tensor extension in the proof of the existing coalgebra-assembly target.

sources.locator: Proposition VI.10.2 and first proof paragraph, pp.232–233
sources.match: Makes the implicit enriched representability and action data explicit without strengthening the printed coequalizer assumption unnoticed.

acceptance: Internal right comodules have underlying object in A and coaction in Ind(A), not arbitrary ind-objects.
Keep the printed reflection-only obligation separate from the sufficient preservation-and-reflection theorem.

api.name: RelativeReconstructionData.action
api.statement: Coherent functor A×C→C with action unit/associativity and the tensor-interchange constraints preserved by F.

api.name: RelativeReconstructionData.representerAdjunction
api.statement: The natural Hom bijections define L_i(V)=V⊙X_i left adjoint to F_i, including unit and counit and both triangle identities.

api.name: RelativeReconstructionData.transition
api.statement: For C_i⊂C_j, representer comparison X_j→X_i corresponds to the unit element in F(X_i), and yields A_j→A_i and A_i∨→A_j∨ compatibly with composition.

api.name: RelativeReconstructionData.internalComodule
api.statement: An H-comodule in A is M∈A with ρ:M→M⊗H in Ind(A) satisfying the counit and coassociativity equations; morphisms intertwine ρ.

api.name: RelativeReconstructionData.preservation
api.statement: The strengthened variant explicitly provides PreservesColimit for each F_i-split parallel pair. Reflection is a different instance.

tests.name: relative_matrix_side
tests.statement: For A=Vect_fd(k), C_i=B-Mod_fd with B=M₂(k) and X_i=B, symmetry gives the left tensor monad B⊗V; its product has E12·E21=E11, detecting B opposite.

tests.name: relative_no_global_representer
tests.statement: The forgetful functor on finite-support Z-graded finite vector spaces has no global finite representer, since a line in a weight outside its finite support has nonzero fibre and no maps from it.

tests.name: relative_weight_pieces
tests.statement: For a finite weight set S, the direct sum of one line in each weight represents the restricted fibre; the local algebra is k^S and the dual coalgebras assemble to k[Z].

tests.name: relative_no_antipode
tests.statement: Finite representations of the affine matrix monoid have the relative reconstruction data but are not rigid; their coefficient bialgebra is not asserted to be Hopf.

uses.how: Pin the action/adjunction and left-module/right-comodule conventions.
Provide relative reconstruction over the rigid coefficient category, without imposing a field or abelianness on A.

nodes.title: Relative reconstruction with preserved split coequalizers
nodes.statement: For the relative reconstruction datum with F_i preserving as well as reflecting all F_i-split coequalizers, the existing finite-piece, coalgebra-assembly and bialgebra targets give a canonical commutative bialgebra H=colim_i F(X_i)∨ in Ind(A) and a symmetric monoidal equivalence C≃Comod_A(H) over A. If C is rigid, its dualities give an antipode on the same H. This theorem makes no assertion that the extra preservation follows from the reflection-only formulation of FS VI.10.2.
hypotheses: The complete action/enriched-representer/filtered-exhaustion datum of relative-reconstruction-datum is supplied.
Each F_i preserves F_i-split coequalizers, and the full inclusions preserve the chosen coequalizers.
proofSteps: Invoke the existing Mathlib Beck theorem on L_i⊣F_i with its separate Has, Preserves and Reflects instances; transport its algebra comparison through F_iL_i(V)≃F(X_i)⊗V.
For a dualizable A_i, transpose the left A_i-action to a right A_i∨-coaction. The algebra product is the one transported from the monad, not an assumed commutative product.

Extend tensor to Ind(A) by filtered colimits. Compactness factors any coaction of an A-object through some A_i∨; after enlarging i, the counit/coassociativity equations hold there. Compactness also factors morphism-intertwining equations. Thus the filtered comparison is essentially surjective and fully faithful.

The Beck presentation by split coequalizers is preserved by tensoring with A and, via conservativity and strong monoidality, by tensoring with C-objects. Choose k containing X_i⊗X_j to prove C_i⊗C_j⊂C_k, then use the existing bialgebra/antipode targets.

sources.match: Proof route with a precisely exposed sufficient additional hypothesis; printed hypothesis comparison stays open.

acceptance: For weight-bounded graded objects H is the direct sum of group-like coefficient lines, with multiplication e_m e_n=e_(m+n), not the pointwise product of finite endomorphism algebras.
For the matrix monoid only the bialgebra conclusion holds; rigidity must precede an antipode.
The ordinary Beck theorem itself is imported, not replanned.

nodes.title: Changing the fibre functor twists the group
nodes.statement: For neutral (C,ω) over k and a fibre functor η over a k-algebra R, let G=Aut⊗(ω) and T=Isom⊗(ω_R,η). Then T is a right G_R-torsor and Aut⊗(η) is the twist of G_R by T for conjugation. Over any faithfully flat R-algebra S with t∈T(S), the isomorphism G_S→Aut⊗(η)_S sends g to t∘g∘t⁻¹. Replacing t by t∘h changes this isomorphism by conjugation by h. Hence over a field the two groups are pure inner forms; no rational point of T is asserted.
hypotheses: η is k-linear exact faithful strong symmetric monoidal with finite projective R-valued fibres.
Composition is ordinary functional composition; T carries right source-group action by precomposition.
proofSteps: Use the existing tensor-isomorphism scheme and torsor theorem to obtain a faithfully flat trivialization.
Define conjugation over the trivialization and compute its transformation on double overlaps: if t₂=t₁∘h then conjugation through t₂ equals conjugation through t₁ after Int(h).
Descend the affine group and its action using the existing fpqc affine descent supplier; identify it with Aut⊗(η) by the functor of points.

sources.match: Fibre torsor and representing algebra, with conjugation descent as the stated consequence.
Consumer needs comparison of crystalline and ordinary fibre groups as pure inner forms; p-adic equivalences remain with their owners.

acceptance: For η=ω_R the identity section gives the original group.
For commutative G conjugation is trivial, so the group twist is canonically G_R even when the fibre torsor is nontrivial.
For GL_n the torsor of frames of a rank-n projective module E twists GL_n to Aut_R(E); do not claim every frame torsor has an R-point.

nodes.title: Artin Nori motives
nodes.statement: For a field k embedded in C, define Art(k) as the rational diagram category of finite étale k-schemes with H⁰_B(X)=Q^{X(C)}, maps by pullback and tensor product induced by X×_kY. Equivalently use zero-dimensional reduced pair vertices in degree zero. Retain its faithful exact fibre, finite direct sums, subquotients and tensor duals. Its fully faithful subquotient-closed inclusion into the full Nori category is a separate target, not a definition.
hypotheses: k has characteristic zero and a chosen embedding k→C; choose an algebraic closure inside C.
Finite étale schemes include disjoint unions; rational coefficients and the ordinary degree-zero symmetry are fixed.
proofSteps: Restrict the MC.5 diagram-category construction and product to zero-dimensional schemes. A relative pair reduces to X minus Y and has cohomology only in degree zero.
Use the identity and evaluation on finite sets to supply tensor unit and products. Rigidity follows from the computed finite Galois Hopf algebras.

sources.match: The actual Nori Artin diagram, rather than the different absolute-Hodge example in DM §6.

acceptance: The empty scheme has zero fibre, Spec(k) has fibre Q, and products correspond to tensor products.

api.name: ArtinNori.ofFiniteEtale
api.statement: Finite étale X gives an object with fibre Q^{Hom_k(X,C)}; a scheme map gives the contravariant cohomology map.

api.name: ArtinNori.product
api.statement: H⁰_B(X×Y)≃H⁰_B(X)⊗H⁰_B(Y), preserving unit and ordinary symmetry.

api.name: ArtinNori.finiteGalois
api.statement: At a finite Galois extension K/k, the diagram category generated by finite Gal(K/k)-sets is equivalent over Q-vector spaces to finite left Q[Gal(K/k)]-modules.

api.name: ArtinNori.embedding
api.statement: The natural faithful exact symmetric monoidal functor to MM_Nori(k,Q) is the functor whose fullness and ambient subquotient closure artin-nori-embedding proves.

tests.name: artin_split
tests.statement: For X=Spec(k) disjoint-union Spec(k), the fibre is Q² with trivial Galois action; this object alone generates the trivial group.

tests.name: artin_quadratic
tests.statement: For a quadratic Galois K/k the fibre of Spec(K) is the two-dimensional permutation representation; rational projectors (1±σ)/2 split it into unit and nontrivial sign lines.

tests.name: artin_regular
tests.statement: For finite Galois K/k with group Γ, the fibre is the regular permutation space Q^Γ and the centralizer of right translations is the left regular Q[Γ]; it is not the full matrix algebra.

tests.name: artin_nongalois
tests.statement: A nonnormal finite extension L/k gives the permutation representation on embeddings Γ/H after passing to a Galois closure; its field automorphism group alone is insufficient.

uses.how: Compute the Artin acceptance example and identify the ambient motivic Galois quotient.

nodes.title: Artin motives and finite-image Galois representations
nodes.statement: Art(k) is symmetrically monoidally equivalent over its Betti fibre to finite-dimensional continuous rational representations of Γ_k=Gal(kbar/k), with the rational vector spaces given the discrete topology. Every such representation factors through a finite quotient. At finite Galois K/k, the diagram endomorphism algebra is Q[Γ] with Δ(g)=g⊗g and ε(g)=1, so its dual coordinate algebra is Q^Γ.
hypotheses: The Artin diagram and rational coefficients of artin-diagram-category are fixed.
proofSteps: For Γ=Gal(K/k), use the simply transitive embedding set of K and its commuting translation actions to compute the endomorphism algebra, including its multiplication side.

Every finite Γ-set is a disjoint union of Γ/H; invariant functions identify Q^{Γ/H} inside Q^Γ. All finite representations are quotients and, by rational Maschke, direct summands of finite sums of the regular representation. Import that semisimplicity, not a new Artin–Wedderburn theory.

Products of finite sets give the diagonal coproduct on Q[Γ]; dualize. Pass through Galois closures and the filtered union of finite Galois extensions. Continuity and compactness of Γ_k imply that the image in discrete GL(V) is finite.

sources.match: Finite diagram algebra, its bialgebra structure and the profinite limit calculation.

acceptance: At a nonabelian finite quotient, left versus right regular multiplication is tested by noncommuting group elements.
Morphisms are Γ-equivariant linear maps; restricting to maps of finite sets would omit rational projectors.

nodes.title: Artin motives form a Nori subcategory
nodes.statement: The natural functor Art(k)→MM_Nori(k,Q) is fully faithful, exact and symmetric monoidal, with image closed under ambient subobjects and quotients. An object of MM_Nori(k,Q) belongs to this image exactly when its base change to kbar is a finite sum of units. Consequently the image is the smallest replete full abelian tensor subcategory generated by H⁰_Nori of finite étale k-schemes.
hypotheses: MC.5 supplies the full rational Nori category, diagram universal property, and the restriction/corestriction and finite-descent contract specified in the request.
proofSteps: Use the equivariant fibre calculation of Proposition 9.4.3 for fullness on generators, and extend through rational projectors and finite sums.

Use corrected Proposition 9.5.3 and Corollary 9.5.5: triviality after algebraic extension descends to a finite extension and exhibits the motive as a summand of a power of H⁰(Spec K). Do not use the false formula res cores(M)=M⊗H⁰(Spec(K⊗_kK)) for arbitrary M.

The unit of the Nori category is simple since its faithful exact fibre is one-dimensional; finite sums of it are ambient semisimple. Base-changing any quotient of an Artin object therefore gives a sum of units, and descent gives an Artin quotient; duality handles subobjects. Semisimplicity of a full subcategory alone would not prove this.

sources.locator: Proposition 9.4.3, p.231; corrected Proposition 9.5.3 and Corollary 9.5.5, pp.232–236; 26 June 2025 repair, pp.238–239
sources.match: Fullness, geometric triviality descent and the repaired ambient subquotient argument.

acceptance: The proof does not infer ambient subquotient closure merely from semisimplicity inside Art(k).
No exact sequence involving the full geometric motivic group is needed as an input to the Artin quotient.

nodes.title: The proconstant Artin motivic Galois group
nodes.statement: For the Betti fibre on Art(k), Aut⊗(ω_B|Art(k)) is the proconstant Q-group scheme lim_K Gal(K/k)_Q, with coordinate Hopf algebra colim_K Q^{Gal(K/k)}. The inclusion of Art(k) induces a faithfully flat morphism G_mot(k,Q)→Γ_k,Q. This is a proalgebraic group scheme; its functor on a disconnected Q-algebra is not defined by assigning the abstract set Γ_k to every algebra.
hypotheses: K ranges over finite Galois extensions in the chosen kbar; the ambient Nori group is reconstructed from its proven neutral fibre.
proofSteps: Compute each finite constant group from the function Hopf algebra, using artin-galois-equivalence.
Take the compatible inverse limit of finite group schemes and apply the existing neutral reconstruction to identify all tensor automorphisms naturally in value algebras.
Apply DM Proposition 2.21 to the fully faithful subquotient-closed inclusion; this proves faithful flatness without assuming a period conjecture.

sources.locator: Section 9.4, p.230; repaired proof of Theorem 9.1.16, pp.236–239

sources.match: Faithfully flat criterion for a tensor subcategory.

acceptance: Over algebraically closed k the group is trivial.
For a finite quotient C₂ and R=Q×Q, R-points are C₂×C₂: independent components detect an incorrectly constant set-valued functor.
For k=Q no assertion of a finite-type algebraic group is made.

nodes.title: The pure Tate tensor subcategory
nodes.statement: Let L=1(−1)=H¹_Nori(G_m,{1}) in the full rational Nori category. For n∈Z put L^n=1(−n), using duals for n<0. Define Tate(k) to be the smallest replete full subcategory containing all L^n and closed under finite sums, subobjects and quotients. Tensor products and duals preserve it by exactness and the invertibility of L. This is the pure Tate subcategory; it is not defined by adjoining every ambient extension.
hypotheses: k⊂C; the full Nori category and its exact faithful tensor Betti fibre are supplied by MC.5.
A Hodge realization separating Tate powers, with type(n,n) on L^n, is supplied as specified in the MC.5 request. Only this separation is used, not a global weight filtration or André semisimplicity.
proofSteps: Use the MC.5 Tate localization for integer powers, coherence maps L^m⊗L^n≃L^(m+n), and L⁰≃1.
One-dimensional faithful exact fibres make every L^n simple. Hodge types imply Hom(L^m,L^n)=0 for m≠n, while End(L^n)=Q by tensoring with the inverse and End(1)=Q.

Subquotients of a finite sum of these ambient simple objects split into the same simples. Thus finite sums already describe Tate(k); do not prove vanishing of all Ext¹ groups in the ambient mixed category.

sources.locator: Definition 10.3.1 and Lemma 10.3.2, pp.250–251; Example 9.1.12, p.213
sources.match: Pure versus extension-closed mixed Tate; the proof uses only Tate separation and finite semisimplicity.
Finite graded vector spaces have the ordinary symmetry used by the G_m example.

acceptance: Degree is n on L^n, so its Hodge weight is 2n and its G_m character is t^n; Q(n)=L^(−n) has character t^(−n).

api.name: PureTate.power
api.statement: For n∈Z the object L^n belongs to Tate(k), with coherent power-zero, addition and duality isomorphisms.

api.name: PureTate.homPower
api.statement: Hom(L^m,L^n)=0 if m≠n and End(L^n)≃Q; all maps between finite sums are block matrices by degree.

api.name: PureTate.sumDecomposition
api.statement: Every object is a finite direct sum of Tate powers, uniquely up to degreewise multiplicity; subobjects and quotients remain such sums.

api.name: PureTate.coefficients
api.statement: M↦(Hom(L^n,M))_n gives finite-support graded rational spaces; tensor on coefficients is the finite convolution of degrees.

api.name: PureTate.mixedBoundary
api.statement: The extension-closed category generated by Tate(k) is the mixed Tate category. No equality with Tate(k) and no G_m calculation for that larger category is asserted.

tests.name: tate_tensor_inverse
tests.statement: L⊗L⁻¹≃1 and the degree-one and degree-minus-one fibres multiply to degree zero; restricting to nonnegative degrees would fail.

tests.name: tate_two_weights
tests.statement: End(1⊕L)=Q×Q and Hom(1,L)=0; replacing it by M₂(Q) would erase the Tate grading.

tests.name: tate_even_symmetry
tests.statement: The self-braiding of L is +1, since its Hodge weight is 2; grading by Tate exponent does not introduce a Koszul minus sign in degree one.

tests.name: tate_extension_boundary
tests.statement: The nontrivial two-dimensional unipotent representation of G_a, with unit subobject and unit quotient, shows why extension closure cannot be silently inserted into a tensor-generated semisimple subcategory definition. This is an abstract categorical counterexample, not a claimed Nori realization.

uses.how: Compute the Tate acceptance example and fix the exponent convention for the period class L.
Use the integer Tate inverse in the formal period ring, with period(L)=2πi.

nodes.title: Pure Tate motives are finite graded vector spaces
nodes.statement: There is a Q-linear symmetric monoidal equivalence Tate(k)≃Vect_fd^Z(Q) over the total Betti fibre, with finite support in Z and ordinary symmetry. It sends L^n to the degree-n line. The inverse sends (V_n) to the finite sum of copowers V_n⊗_Q L^n. There is no Koszul sign from the Tate-exponent grading.
hypotheses: The definition and Tate separation of pure-tate-subcategory are supplied.
Fix the Betti generator of L from the positively oriented loop to identify the total fibre with the ordinary forgetful fibre; alternative choices transport the equivalence coherently.
proofSteps: Use the computed Hom spaces of Tate powers to identify maps with degree-preserving block matrices.

nodes.title: The Tate group is the multiplicative group
nodes.statement: For every commutative Q-algebra R, tensor automorphisms of the Betti fibre restricted to Tate(k) are naturally Rˣ: a∈Rˣ acts on L^n by a^n, and every tensor automorphism has this form. Thus the coordinate Hopf algebra is Q[t,t⁻¹], Δ(t)=t⊗t, ε(t)=1, S(t)=t⁻¹, and the group is G_m,Q. The full motivic group maps faithfully flatly to this Tate quotient.
hypotheses: The pure Tate equivalence and ambient subquotient closure are fixed; all value algebras, including disconnected and nonreduced ones, are tested.
proofSteps: Naturality on each finite-dimensional pure degree and all its linear maps forces a scalar a_n; monoidality gives a_(m+n)=a_ma_n and the unit forces a_0=1.
The inverse-degree line forces a_1 to be a unit and a_n=a_1^n. Conversely these scalars define a tensor automorphism and commute with value-algebra maps.
Use the existing G_m affine Hopf dictionary rather than rebuilding the diagonalizable-group theory. Apply DM 2.21(a) to the full ambient subquotient-closed Tate inclusion.

retainedTargetRefinements.statement: Let D be a graded diagram with commutative product structure and unit, and T_1, T_2 two unital graded multiplicative representations of D in finite dimensional vector spaces over Q (the source works over Q; the construction uses only that Q is a field). The comparison algebra is A_{1,2} = colim_F Hom(T_1|F, T_2|F)^∨, the filtered colimit over finite subdiagrams F of the duals of the spaces of families of linear maps T_1(p) → T_2(p), p in F, commuting with the edges of F. It is a commutative Q-algebra, with multiplication induced as for the tensor structure of the diagram category (Proposition B.16) with Hom(T_1|F, T_2|F) in place of End(T|F). Precomposition by End(T_1|F) gives a right source action and its coordinate coaction A_{1,2}→A_{1,2}⊗A_1. Postcomposition by End(T_2|F) gives a left target action and coaction A_{1,2}→A_2⊗A_{1,2}. These statements use ordinary functional composition. For T_1=T_2=T the algebra is A(D,T).

apiReplacements.ComparisonAlgebra.comul: The source-group coaction A_{1,2}→A_{1,2}⊗A_1 is dual to precomposition x∘g_1.

retainedTargetRefinements.statement: In the setting of Section 3, with T_1 and T_2 unital graded multiplicative representations of the same diagram over Q, a multiplicative comparison isomorphism over a field K ⊃ Q and C(T_1) neutral Tannakian, let T_2 also denote its extension to a tensor fibre functor on C(T_1) (MC.6/fibre-functor-extension). The functor on commutative Q-algebras R ↦ Iso⊗(T_1 ⊗ R, T_2 ⊗ R) is represented by the affine scheme X_{1,2} = Spec A_{1,2}, and likewise X_{2,1} = Spec A_{2,1}. Composition gives X_{1,2}×X_{2,1}→G_2 by (x,y)↦x∘y and X_{2,1}×X_{1,2}→G_1 by (y,x)↦y∘x. The target group G_2 acts on the left, G_2×X_{1,2}→X_{1,2}, by postcomposition, and the source group G_1 on the right, X_{1,2}×G_1→X_{1,2}, by precomposition.

apiReplacements.TensorIsoScheme.compLeft: The morphism G_2×X_{1,2}→X_{1,2}, (g,x)↦g∘x, dually the target-group coaction A_{1,2}→A_2⊗A_{1,2}.
apiReplacements.TensorIsoScheme.compRight: The morphism X_{1,2}×G_1→X_{1,2}, (x,g)↦x∘g, dually the source-group coaction A_{1,2}→A_{1,2}⊗A_1.
apiReplacements.TensorIsoScheme.toAut: The morphism X_{1,2}×X_{2,1}→G_2, (x,y)↦x∘y; the reversed composition has target G_1.

testReplacements.TensorIsoScheme.compose_inverse: For x:T_1→T_2, x∘x⁻¹ is the unit of G_2 and x⁻¹∘x is the unit of G_1. The action g_2∘x and action x∘g_1 are defined, fixing the side by types.

proofSteps: Describe the R-points of Spec A_{1,2}: algebra maps A_{1,2} → R are compatible families, over finite subdiagrams F, of R-linear maps T_1|F ⊗ R → T_2|F ⊗ R commuting with the edges and respecting the product structure, by the duality defining A_{1,2}.

Identify such families with tensor morphisms f_{T_1} ⊗ R → T_2 ⊗ R on C(T_1), using that C(T_1) is generated by the objects attached to vertices (Proposition B.9) and its description by finite comodules.

Show that every tensor morphism is an isomorphism, by rigidity and Deligne and Milne's Proposition 1.13 (the second step of MC.6/rigid-bialgebra-is-hopf), so that the functor of tensor isomorphisms is represented by Spec A_{1,2}.
Composition gives the target coaction A_{1,2}→A_2⊗A_{1,2} and source coaction A_{1,2}→A_{1,2}⊗A_1; the two opposite-order composition maps are dual to A_2→A_{1,2}⊗A_{2,1} and A_1→A_{2,1}⊗A_{1,2}.

retainedTargetRefinements.statement: Let C be a neutral Tannakian category over a field k with fibre functor ω and G = Aut⊗(ω), and let η be a fibre functor on C with values in a commutative k-algebra R. Then the functor Hom⊗(ω, η) on R-algebras is represented by an affine scheme faithfully flat over Spec R, every tensor morphism from ω to η is an isomorphism, and Hom⊗(ω, η) is a G-torsor over R. The G_R-action is on the right by precomposition. The category may be any neutral datum: use neutral-tannaka-reconstruction to reach the finite-comodule model before applying the known-Hopf dictionary.
